Return-value mappings and payload JSON options

Source: R/mcplite-results.R
mcplite-results.Rd

Tools can return ordinary R values for text conversion, or tool_result() for explicit MCP content and structured data. This topic defines the shared serialization contract. See tool_result() for construction and fallback, and mcp_server() under "Protocol compatibility" for version projection.

Ordinary return values

Character scalars become literal text and character vectors are joined with newlines. Other JSON-serializable values become JSON in one text content block. Bare lists are ordinary values, not MCP result objects. Ordinary NULL becomes the text "{}"; an ordinary unnamed list() becomes "[]".

For per-tool conversion choices, return your own JSON as ordinary character text, for example as.character(jsonlite::toJSON(value, na = "null")). JSON-looking strings and jsonlite json objects are never parsed or inserted as raw JSON. In structured_content, they remain string values.

Structured-content mappings

Structured values follow jsonlite::toJSON() and the payload options below, with one root convention: a bare empty list at the structured root represents {}. Nested unnamed empty lists retain jsonlite's [] mapping. NULL means absence of the structured-content field, not a JSON null value.

With default options:

R valueStructured-content meaning
list(ok = TRUE)JSON object
c("a", "b")JSON array
"done"JSON string scalar, not parsed as JSON
list() or structure(list(), names = character())Empty object {}
I(list())Explicit empty array []
NA or NA_character_JSON null
NA_integer_, NA_real_, or NA_complex_JSON string "NA"
NULLNo structured-content field

Classes, dimensions, and explicit I() or jsonlite::unbox() representations retain their jsonlite mappings. Tool authors are responsible for conformance with any advertised output schema.

Payload JSON options

Configure these package-global R options before constructing results and starting the server, and keep them stable while the server runs:

  • mcplite.json.null: "null" (default) or "list". Named payload NULL fields remain present, as JSON null or {}, respectively.

  • mcplite.json.na: unset by default, which omits jsonlite's na argument and preserves its class-specific defaults. Set "null" or "string" to select that jsonlite mapping. "null" also maps NaN and infinities to JSON null and retains missing data-frame fields instead of omitting them.

  • mcplite.json.auto_unbox: TRUE (default) or FALSE. Setting FALSE keeps singleton payload vectors as arrays; explicit I() and jsonlite::unbox() representations still apply.

Remove an option with NULL, for example options(mcplite.json.na = NULL), to restore its default. This omits na; it does not forward na = NULL. These options apply to ordinary noncharacter return-value JSON and to structured content, its representability checks, generated text fallback, and protocol-version projection. Protocol fields, schemas, annotations, and all result and content metadata retain fixed encoding.

See also

mcplite, tool_result(), content_text()

Examples

local({
  old <- options(mcplite.json.na = "null", mcplite.json.auto_unbox = FALSE)
  on.exit(options(old))
  result <- tool_result(structured_content = list(
    count = 1L,
    values = c(NA_real_, NaN, Inf, -Inf),
    rows = data.frame(id = 1L, missing = NA_real_)
  ))
  result$content[[1]]$text
})
#> [1] "{\"count\":[1],\"values\":[null,null,null,null],\"rows\":[{\"id\":1,\"missing\":null}]}"
